$comment: Test files that do not yet pass on Windows. The `windows-unit` CI job runs the ENTIRE unit suite
on windows-latest — nothing is filtered — and scripts/windows-unit-report.mjs judges the result
against this list (issue #434). Before that job, exactly one test file ran on Windows.
The list is enforced in BOTH directions from that single run: a failing file that is not listed
is a new regression and fails the job; a listed file with zero failures has been fixed and also
fails the job, so the entry must be deleted. That keeps this a shrinking backlog rather than a
permanent hole, and keeps the job a real gate rather than a test of the list itself.
It is a deny-list on purpose: a NEW test file runs on Windows unless someone deliberately names
it here. An allow-list would leave every future file uncovered by default, which is how the
`suspectedProductionBug` marks entries whose failure shows a platform separator inside a value
the product PERSISTS or SERVES (an artifact, a spec reference, a generated path) rather than
inside a test expectation. Those are portability questions about the artifact, not test bugs,

`flaky: true` marks an entry that is NOT deterministically failing — it is exempt from both rules, because a file that oscillates would otherwise fail the build whichever list it sits on. It is a last resort: it needs observed evidence in its reason, it is reported on every run so it stays visible, and it belongs in the backlog issue as a bug to fix rather than a state to keep.

exclusions.reason: ONE case: 'reports no analysis in progress for a stale lock'. Re-listed after being removed too eagerly on one machine's evidence — it passes 5/5 on a Windows 11 developer box and fails on the runner, so local green is not sufficient here. What the run shows: the assertion on line 138 PASSES (isOwnershipStale returns true for the planted lock) and line 139 fails, so openloreAnalysisStatus disagrees with the predicate the test says it must match, milliseconds apart on the same file. The likely difference is PID liveness for a just-exited child: deadPid() returns the pid after 'exit', but a Windows process can still be opened while a handle survives, so isProcessAlive may answer true in one call and false in the other. NOT confirmed - stated as the hypothesis to test first, not as the diagnosis. Same neighbourhood as the analysis-ownership SIGTERM case.

FLAKY on Windows, not deterministically failing — observed failing at commit e8d6c8dd and again on the following run, then PASSING on the next run of the same tree. Surfaced BY this PR rather than caused by it: the failures are the 100-way concurrency cases, and they began once the deny-list stopped skipping ~47 files and the job started doing several times the work. One root cause, not three — the first case times out mid-lock and the next two then fail on the gate it left behind (`NamespaceGateHeldError`). Verified present before this PR touched `atomic-store.ts`, which only exported an existing function. Green on Linux CI and in isolation on macOS. Flaky rather than plain-listed because a file that oscillates fails the build whichever list it sits on. The fix is a longer budget for these cases on Windows or a gate released on timeout; tracked in #452 as a bug, not a state to keep.
